vs_published_round2._not_only_the_convention_moved: The organ MASKS are not the same masks. The reference is: on LiTS and MSD the per-case reference organ volume agrees with round 2's to better than 0.01 cm3 on every case. The PREDICTION is not: it differs on every case, and ours is systematically the larger. The two arms are two different TotalSegmentator invocations - the masks scored here were written by src/eval/baseline.py's run_totalsegmentator, which runs ts_runner in a clean subprocess with task 'total', fast=True and NO roi_subset, on the local 1080 Ti, and remaps to the unified space at write time; the pipeline team round 3 section 10 records his as the Python API with fast=True, ml=True and roi_subset of seven classes. So the movement between round 2's organ cell and this one is NOT a pure convention change and must never be presented as one. What this table legitimately claims is that THE AUTONOMOUS ORGAN COLUMN NOW HAS A STATED CONVENTION and travels with its parenchyma pair - not that convention A raised or lowered a number by the difference shown.
vs_published_round2._why_kits_moves: Measured, not assumed, and the first thing the measurement did was refute the explanation we expected to give. (1) THE REFERENCE DID NOT MOVE. Our pooled parenchyma reference matches round 2's tumour-excluded reference to better than 0.01 cm3 on all 36 cohort cases. The laterality repair fires on 35 of them - it is not a no-op - but what it restores is exactly the dataset's own whole kidney, which is what round 2 scored against too. The 5,000-voxel splitter defect was a defect of the PER-SIDE reference, and this table does not use a per-side reference. (2) THE PREDICTION DID MOVE, and that is the whole of the parenchyma gap: 0.8356 against round 2's 0.8748 with an identical reference means a different organ mask, and ours is larger by 74.3 cm3 on average - a different TotalSegmentator invocation, not a different convention. (3) THE CYST RULING MOVES THE CONVENTION-A COLUMN ONLY, and on this cohort it is material: 16 of the 36 KiTS cohort cases carry a reference cyst, and on each of those the ruling adds the cyst to the organ-with-mass reference while leaving the parenchyma reference alone. It cannot explain any part of the parenchyma difference, and it is not offered as doing so.

convention_A: CONVENTION A. prediction = the organ model ALONE; reference = the organ label UNION the mass components attributed to that organ by host attribution. The prediction is never unioned with a predicted tumour and never carved by one: an organ score measures the organ model. Emitted as organ_dice and, under its older name, dice_organ_with_mass - the same number.
parenchyma: parenchyma_dice is Dice against the organ label with the mass removed; parenchyma_recall is |P and parenchyma| / |parenchyma|. Published with every organ_with_mass figure: at case_00067's left-kidney mass fraction of 0.888 a prediction of the mass alone scores 0.941 organ-with-mass while recovering zero parenchyma, and only the recall separates the two.
mass_coverage: |P and host mass| / |host mass|, where the host mass is the part of the organ-with-mass reference that is mass. How much of the reference mass the ORGAN prediction actually covers. With parenchyma_recall it separates 'the model found the organ' from 'the model found the tumour and called it the organ': the degenerate mass-alone prediction scores coverage 1.000 and recall 0.000. None, not zero, when the organ hosts no mass - there is nothing to cover.
cyst_ruling: KiTS23 cyst (native class 3, unified 15) is counted INTO the kidney: it is part of the organ-with-mass reference exactly as the tumour is, it is excluded from the parenchyma reference exactly as the tumour is, and it is one of the 'host mass' voxels that mass_coverage measures and that the lesion-as-ignore-region reading drops. Advisor decision, 2026-10-03. Every artefact that scores KiTS reports the cyst-bearing count of its own sample, because this ruling moves every case that has one and no case that has not.
arm: autonomous: organ = TotalSegmentator v2 --fast (3 mm), unified label space; the organ model's own mask, never unioned with or carved by a predicted tumour
semi_oracle_cannot_follow: The cohort SEMI-ORACLE organ row cannot be moved to convention A. the pipeline team round 3 item 3: the single-organ cohort's semi-oracle masks did not survive the 18/19 September wipe - the masks behind the frozen records were never retained, the 09-17 regenerations were on the wiped scratch disk, and the organ test-set masks behind the organ tables were never saved, only their metrics. Convention A needs the MASK (it changes the reference, not the arithmetic on a stored Dice), so the semi-oracle single-organ cohort row stays TUMOUR-EXCLUDED and must be labelled as such. Only FLARE23's 576 semi-oracle masks survive; the pipeline team has offered to re-score that one collection under convention A, and to re-run the three single-organ lists on the surviving organ checkpoints at about 1 GPU-hour.
